title: Reconcile Selection
prompt: A React table keeps selected row ids in state, but rows can disappear after filtering. Write a helper that returns only selected ids that still exist in the current rows, preserving the selection order.

explanation.beginner:
Example: reconcileSelection(["a","b","c"], [{"id":"a"},{"id":"c"}]) produces ["a","c"]. Evaluate the selection rule for every record and preserve the qualifying values in the required order.

Compare “returns empty when nothing remains”: input [["x"],[{"id":"a"}]] produces []. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Evaluate the selection rule for every record and preserve the qualifying values in the required order.

Tempting mistake: Selecting a display position after a list changes can identify the wrong item. Use the domain key when matching two collections.

The reference uses map, filter. Trace the intermediate value after each operation; count repeated scans inside callbacks separately when estimating cost.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “returns empty when nothing remains”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
